chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Ali ibn Hadid from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Dawud ibn al-Husayn and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab and al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Dawud ibn al-Husayn from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in a long hadith, he said:

"The testimony of women is not valid for the breaking of the fast (Fitr) except the testimony of two just men, and there is no objection to the testimony of women for fasting, even if it is one woman."
From Hilal, that her testimony is not accepted in the entire will, although it is permissible to accept it for the quarter, as we have clarified.

key_terms.الْفِطْرِ: Breaking of the fast (specifically Eid al-Fitr/moon sighting)

ai.seo_question: What is the validity of a woman's testimony for confirming the start of Ramadan or Eid compared to a man's testimony in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* delineates the jurisprudential distinction between public religious observances and private legal transactions, ruling that women's testimony is insufficient for the communal sighting of the moon to end Ramadan unless corroborated by two just men. Conversely, it validates a single woman's testimony for confirming fasting days and limits her acceptance in wills to a specific portion, reflecting the Shia scholarly view on the varying evidentiary weight of gender in different legal contexts.
